read_from: photo 0 label (partially legible, brand visible, number unclear)

risks.risk: Alternator may not charge or may have worn brushes/bearings (common failure points in used units).
risks.proof: A bench test clip showing the pulley spinning with a multimeter reading charging voltage (13.5-14.5V).

risks.risk: Visible seam/crack line across the housing in photos 1 and 2 could be a structural crack rather than a casting seam.
risks.proof: A close-up photo of that seam line from multiple angles to confirm it is factory casting, not damage.

risks.risk: Corrosion and dust buildup on windings (photo 1) may indicate water exposure or long storage, risking insulation breakdown.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of windings after cleaning, or a resistance/insulation test reading.

risks.risk: Part number and fitment to M278 cannot be confirmed, risking wrong-engine mismatch.
risks.proof: Clear close-up photo of the full label/part number, or OEM sticker matched against M278 parts catalog.
risks.if_unproven: priced as unconfirmed fitment, generic used alternator

proof_requests: Clear, well-lit close-up of the Valeo label showing the full part number.
Bench test video showing the pulley spinning and a voltage reading under load.
Close-up of the seam/crack line on the housing from two angles.
Photo of the connector pins and wiring harness end for corrosion check.
response.reason: The item is identifiable by type and visible brand (Valeo alternator) but functional and fitment claims are unverified, and a possible housing crack and winding corrosion are visible, so it must be priced at worst case as an untested, possibly damaged used alternator.
